label: Chunk, embed, index
summary: Turns documents into chunks, vectors and a BM25 keyword index that retrieval searches.

children.label: Embedder
children.summary: ABC that turns texts into normalized vectors; model classes are interchangeable.

children.label: embedder.py
children.summary: Embedder ABC, MiniLM and gte-modernbert implementations, EMBEDDERS registry.
children.details:
- `MiniLmEmbedder`: all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384 dimensions, reads 256 tokens, batch 128.
- `GteModernBertEmbedder`: gte-modernbert-base, 768 dimensions, reads 8,192 tokens, runs in float16 with batch 4 and casts vectors back to float32.
- `EMBEDDERS`: maps the CLI names `minilm` and `gte` to the classes.

children.label: Strategy + registry
children.summary: Pipelines take any Embedder; EMBEDDERS maps CLI names (minilm, gte) to classes, and dimensions pick the table set.
children.details: Pipelines (`run_data_ingestion`, `index_summaries`) take any `Embedder` and never name a model. `EMBEDDERS` in `embedder.py` maps the CLI names `minilm` and `gte` to classes. The embedder's `name` picks the chunker in `CHUNKERS`, and its `dimensions` picks the table set in `EMBEDDING_TABLES` (384 -> `embeddings`, 768 -> `embeddings_768`), so switching models switches size, tables and chunk length together.

Contract: an `Embedder` has class-level `name`, `dimensions` and `max_tokens`, and one method `embed(texts) -> list[list[float]]` returning one unit-length vector per text, in order. Unit length means cosine distance ranks results.

A new model needs those three attributes, an `embed` that normalizes, an entry in `EMBEDDERS`, and a matching vector size in `tables/embedding.py` and a chunk size in `CHUNKERS` of the ingestion pipeline.

children.label: Chunk pipeline
children.summary: Resumable batch pipeline: load, parse, normalize, chunk, embed, store per document.

children.label: data_ingestion.py
children.summary: run_data_ingestion: plans pending documents and commits each batch of 500.
children.details: `run_data_ingestion` plans the pending documents per source type (`pending_documents`), then loops batches through the six steps. `CHUNKERS` holds a `RecursiveChunker` per model name. `forget_list_documents` deletes chunks of documents stored as a list literal so they become pending and are re-embedded from decoded text.

children.label: chunking.py
children.summary: RecursiveChunker cuts at paragraph, line, sentence, word, adding neighbour context.
children.details: `RecursiveChunker.split` cuts text at `SEPARATORS` (paragraph, line, sentence, space), recursing into pieces over `size`, and `merge` joins neighbours back up to `size`; a piece with no break left is cut hard at `size`. `chunks` prepends the title and adds `context` characters from the previous chunk's tail and next chunk's head (`tail`, `head`, cut at word boundaries). `chunk_documents` wraps the texts as `Chunk` models with a `position`.

children.label: Chunk size per model
children.summary: MiniLM reads 256 tokens so chunks are 600 chars; gte reads 8,192 so most documents stay whole.
children.details: `CHUNKERS` in `data_ingestion.py` comments: sizes are in characters at about 3.7 characters per token. MiniLM reads 256 word pieces, so `RecursiveChunker(size=600, context=100)`: 600 characters plus 100 of context each side and the title fit in 95% of chunks. gte-modernbert reads 8,192 tokens, so `size=24_000, context=500` keeps most documents whole.

children.label: Resume by absence
children.summary: A document with chunks from the model counts as done, so a stopped run just restarts; the vector index is dropped during load and rebuilt after.
children.details: `pending_documents` returns documents with no rows for this model and field (`embedded_document_ids`), so a document is done once any chunk is stored. Each batch is stored and committed together, so a stop loses at most one batch and a rerun just plans what is left. The vector index is dropped per source before loading and rebuilt after (`drop_vector_index`, `create_vector_index`), so a large load does not update the index row by row.

The main path: documents are processed per source type in batches of `DOCUMENT_BATCH = 500`, each batch committed in one transaction.

Steps per batch: `load_documents`, `parse_documents` (parsed fields upserted to `parsed_documents`), `normalize_documents`, `chunk_documents`, `embedder.embed`, `store_chunks`. Before the first batch of a source the vector index is dropped; after its last batch `create_vector_index` rebuilds the StreamingDiskANN index.

Options: `sample` limits to the test sample (cited documents plus N distractors), `fresh` deletes the model's chunks first, `redo_lists` re-embeds documents stored as list literals. Progress is recorded for `train-rag progress-page`.

children.label: Summary index
children.summary: Embeds summaries the documents already carry instead of chunking them.

children.label: index_summaries.py
children.summary: index_summaries: embeds Fireflies, GitHub and Jira free summaries under field summary.
children.details: `index_summaries` loops `FREE_SUMMARIES` (source type -> parsed attribute name), builds table records with `field='summary'` and position 0, and replaces the model's old rows. Prints counts and seconds per source.

children.label: Cheap first iteration
children.summary: The first iteration favours searching summaries over chunking every document; free summaries cost no LLM.
children.details: The brainstorm doc proposes searching summaries first rather than chunking every document; the summaries already exist in the parsed fields, so this index costs only embedding time and no LLM calls.

Skips chunking: for Fireflies (`summary`), GitHub (`description`) and Jira (`issue_summary`) the parser's free summary field is embedded as one text per document under field `summary`. Other sources have no such field and are skipped. Defaults to `MiniLmEmbedder`.

Per source: parse each artifact, collect (document id, doc id, summary), embed all at once, `replace_embeddings` for that model and field, then `create_vector_index`. Retrieval can search the `summary` field instead of `chunk`.

children.label: BM25 index
children.summary: Keyword index over whole documents, saved to disk instead of the database.

children.label: index_bm25.py
children.summary: index_bm25: stemmed bm25s index plus documents.json, per all or sample folder.
children.details: `index_bm25` tokenizes per source and batch, builds the vocabulary and corpus, calls `model.index((corpus, vocabulary))` and saves. `tokenize` wraps `bm25s.tokenize`. `bm25_index_dir` names the output folder by sample.

children.label: Words as int ids
children.summary: Tokens are stored as ids in compact arrays because about 300M words as strings would not fit in memory.
children.details: In `index_bm25`, a comment says the corpus (about 300M words) would not fit in memory as Python strings. Each word is mapped to an int id via `vocabulary.setdefault(word, len(vocabulary))` and each document stored as an `array('i')`; bm25s accepts the `(corpus, vocabulary)` pair directly.

A lexical alternative to the vector tables. Each document's normalized title plus content is tokenized (lowercase, English stopwords removed, Snowball-stemmed via `Stemmer`) and indexed with `bm25s`. Output goes to `data/bm25/all` or `data/bm25/sample_<n>`: the bm25s files plus `documents.json`, a list of `IndexedDocument` (document id, doc id, source type) in index order so hits map back to documents.

Documents load in batches of 5,000 per source type. Whole documents are indexed, not chunks.

children.label: Also uses
children.summary: Chunk model and embedding storage the indexers write through.

children.label: models/chunk.py
children.summary: Chunk and CleanDocument models passed between steps.
children.details: Pydantic models: `CleanDocument` (document_id, doc_id, title, text) leaves normalization; `Chunk` (document_id, doc_id, position, text) leaves chunking.

children.label: tables/embedding.py
children.summary: Embedding tables per source type and vector dimension.
children.details: `EmbeddingRecord` has document_id, doc_id, field, position, previous_id, next_id, model, text, embedding. `MiniEmbeddingRecord` is Vector(384), `BaseEmbeddingRecord` Vector(768). `BASES` and `source_table` build one table per source type and size; names are `embeddings` and `embeddings_768`.

children.label: repository/embedding.py
children.summary: Pending-document query, chunk storage and vector index create/drop.
children.details: Write side: `pending_documents`, `store_chunks` (reserves row ids with `reserve_ids`, then `neighbour_ids` fills previous_id/next_id), `replace_embeddings`, `delete_embeddings`, `delete_document_embeddings`, `create_vector_index` (pgvectorscale diskann, cosine) and `drop_vector_index`. Also holds `search_embeddings`, used by retrieval.
Supporting files the ingestion code writes through: the models passed between steps, the table definitions and the database functions for chunks and vector indexes.

children.label: Neighbour context
children.summary: Chunks carry neighbour text so later steps can send a chunk with its neighbours, not whole documents, cutting LLM tokens.
children.details: Two kinds of neighbour context exist. Text: `RecursiveChunker.chunks` adds the tail of the previous chunk and the head of the next (100 characters for MiniLM) so a mid-topic chunk still says its topic. Links: `store_chunks` stores `previous_id` and `next_id` per row, so a retrieval step can send a hit with its neighbours instead of the whole document. The cost-savings article argues this cuts LLM tokens.

details:
Produces the searchable data that retrieval reads: embedding rows in Postgres (pgvector tables, one per source type and vector size) and an on-disk BM25 keyword index.

Three entry points, each a CLI command:
- `train-rag ingest` runs `run_data_ingestion`: load, parse, normalize, chunk, embed, store, in batches of 500 documents.
- `train-rag index-summaries` embeds the summaries Fireflies, GitHub and Jira documents already carry.
- `train-rag index-bm25` tokenizes whole documents into a stemmed `bm25s` index under `data/bm25/`.

Documents come from the `documents` table loaded earlier (EnterpriseRAG-Bench loader); parsing and normalizing reuse the parsers and `processing/normalize.py`. Output goes to the retrieval modules, which search `embeddings` / `embeddings_768` and the BM25 folder.

Read `pipelines/data_ingestion.py` first, then `embedder.py`.
